To find ${g}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{x-{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2xy}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{x-{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{(x-{y}^{2})-x}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{{y}^{2}}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y)+{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{2xy}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}}+(-\frac{{y}^{2}}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2xy-{y}^{2}}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{y(2x-y)}{(x-{y}^{2})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
